bull.t: Low Leverage And Improved Equity Base
bull.b: The very low debt burden reduces solvency pressure and preserves flexibility while the Whistler project advances. Substantial improvement in equity from earlier negative levels indicates recapitalization has strengthened the capital base, although continuing losses may consume that support over time.

bull.t: Whistler Exploration Is Expanding The Resource Opportunity
bull.b: New mineralized outcrops, expanded interpreted footprints, and additional drill targets can strengthen the long-term development case for Whistler. The work also supports continued resource growth efforts around an existing multi-million-ounce gold-equivalent resource base, subject to further drilling.

bull.t: Regional Infrastructure And Permitting Support Is Advancing
bull.b: Improving road, rail, power, and port connectivity could reduce a major development hurdle for the remote Whistler project and improve the economics of the wider corridor. Federal and state support provides a durable infrastructure pathway, though construction and permitting remain ongoing.

bear.b: Without operating revenue, U.S. GoldMining cannot currently fund exploration from internally generated earnings. The sharp increase in TTM losses indicates heavier cash requirements and reduces near-term financial self-sufficiency, leaving project advancement dependent on capital access and eventual development success.

bear.t: Persistent Negative Cash Flow Increases Funding Dependence
bear.b: Ongoing cash burn means the company must continue financing exploration, studies, permitting, and corporate costs before any mine generates revenue. Although TTM free cash flow improved versus prior annual periods, the consistently negative profile increases funding and potential dilution risk over the next several quarters.

bear.t: Nasdaq Audit Committee Compliance Remains Unresolved
bear.b: The unresolved audit committee deficiency creates a governance and listing-compliance burden that management must address while the project remains pre-revenue. Reconstituting the committee within the cure period is necessary to restore Nasdaq compliance and maintain confidence in oversight structures.
